title: Attestation orchestration and log schema brainstorm
content:
Purpose:
This is a working brain-dump for automating access attestation (quarterly) tied directly to RBAC v2, our audit-log schema, and downstream SIEM exports. Focus: make evidence collection repeatable & auditable for internal reviewers and external auditors while keeping operational overhead low.

High-level goals:
- Define minimal attestation slice: who has privileged roles, why, and when last approved.
- Source-of-truth: RBAC v2 role assignments in Identity DB + binding metadata (owner, justification, expiry).
- Evidence pipeline: daily audit-log export -> transform -> SIEM ingest -> snapshot export for auditor bundles.
- Automate reminders and revocations for expired/unused privileges.

Current constraints / context:
- RBAC v2 rollout scheduled for Jan 2026; pilot teams (infra, sre, se) migrated.
- Audit logs emitted from API gateway, control plane, and private deploys. Log schema is converging but still has subtle variant names (actor_id vs user_id).
- SIEMs in use: Splunk for infra/security, Elastic for application telemetry, Datadog for some SaaS tenants. We need a canonical export format that all three can consume.

Proposed attestation orchestration flow (draft):
1) Period boundary triggered (quarterly Cron on orchestration service).
2) Query RBAC v2 for all active bindings with scope >= privileged-level (privileged-level = roles in privileged role-set). Include fields: binding_id, principal_id, principal_type, role_id, scope (org/team/resource), justification_text, granted_by, granted_at, expiration_ts, last_activity_ts.
3) Pull deterministic activity evidence: last_activity_ts from audit logs (last 90/180/365 days).
4) Enrich bindings with manager/owner and ticket links (if present in metadata).
5) Compile attestable list and split by owner; for each owner create an attestation artifact that lists bindings and recommended action (keep/revoke/rotate).
6) Publish tasks to Attestation UI and send email/Slack alert with CTA and 2-week SLA.
7) After grace period, automate low-risk revocation for bindings with no response and last_activity_ts > 180 days (policy configurable).
8) Snapshot final evidence bundle (RBAC export CSV + activity excerpts + audit-log SID markers) and push to auditor S3 bucket (encrypted, retention 7 years).

Audit log schema (canonical) - required fields (proposal):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- event_id: uuid
- service: short name (api-gateway | control-plane | private-agent)
- event_type: action semantic (auth:role.grant | auth:role.revoke | model:deploy | kv:cache.hit | routing:route.fallback)
- actor_id: unique actor (user:<id> | service:<id> | key:<id>)
- actor_type: user | service | api_key
- target_resource: fully-qualified resource id (e.g., org/123/project/456/cluster/abc)
- role_id: if event pertains to RBAC assignment (nullable)
- binding_id: if event pertains to binding lifecycle
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- client_ip: optional, masked if PII policy requires
- request_id: correlation id for tracing across services
- extra: free-text, must be JSON-string escaped in final CSV/NDJSON export

Notes on schema choices:
- Use actor_id normalized to include type prefix to avoid cross-service collisions.
- request_id must be propagated end-to-end; many gaps exist today. One engineering task: add middleware to propagate request_id from edge into control-plane events.
- outcome values are important for auditors to see failed privilege escalations.

SIEM export format and ingestion notes:
- Export as NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) for Elastic & Splunk universal forwarder; also support gzipped archives for batch S3 drops.
- Daily export job should partition by date and service (s3://redwood-audit-exports/{env}/{service}/YYYY/MM/DD/). Use server-side KMS encryption and IAM role scoping.
- Include a small index (manifest.json) per partition with counts and md5 checksums for integrity checks.

Evidence automation checklist (for quarterly run):
- [ ] Confirm RBAC v2 bindings API endpoint readiness (endpoint: /rbac/v2/bindings?since=DATE).
- [ ] Run daily audit-log enrichment to populate last_activity_ts for each binding.
- [ ] Verify request_id propagation for at least control-plane and api-gateway (JIRA: SEC-4212).
- [ ] Implement attestation UI email templates + Slack workflow (channel #access-attest).
- [ ] Build CI job to snapshot attestation run and push bundle to S3 with retention tags.
- [ ] Add automated revocation lambda for expired and inactive bindings (must require 2 sign-off for high-impact roles).
- [ ] Create Splunk saved searches and Elastic dashboards used by auditors.

Sample Splunk query (privileged access activity last 90 days):
index=audits service="control-plane" event_type="auth:role.grant" OR event_type="auth:role.revoke" | stats latest(timestamp) as last_seen by actor_id, role_id | where last_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-90d")

Sample Elastic/KQL (failed admin escalations):
service:control-plane AND event_type:"auth:role.grant" AND outcome:failure | sort by timestamp desc | limit 100

Edge cases / open questions:
- How do we treat service accounts vs human users in attestation workflows? Proposal: separate flows and SLAs; service accounts require owner + runbook link; human owners get normal attestation tasks.
- RBAC bindings created by automation (CI/CD) need ticket linkage; if missing, auto-tag as 'bot-created' and require runbook reference.
- Partial events (outcome=partial) — we should include these in evidence and add follow-up actions; auditors tend to flag partials.
- Multi-cloud private deployments: ensure audit collector config is per-customer and that we can only surface metadata allowed by contract (no cross-tenant leakage).

Retention & privacy considerations:
- Evidence bundles stored in auditor S3 should be encrypted with dedicated KMS key and retention policy 7 years for privileged access reviews.
- Mask client_ip above /24 when exported for auditor environments unless explicit justification.
- Redact sensitive request payloads; only include metadata and relevant identifiers in auditor bundle.

Operational runbook (short):
- 00:00 (day 0): Orchestration cron triggers attestation-run job.
- 00:01: Query RBAC v2 bindings and enrich with last_activity_ts.
- 00:10: Generate per-owner attestation tasks; send Slack/email.
- Day 14: Reminder 1 (automated).
- Day 21: Reminder 2 + Escalation to manager.
- Day 28: Apply automated revocation policy for low-risk items. Create MR for high-impact revocations for manual approval.
- Post-run: push evidence bundle to s3://redwood-auditor-bundles/{run-id}.zip and post summary to #sec-audits channel.

Implementation tasks (owners suggested):
- RBAC API + binding export: Marcus Lee (eng-identity) — SEC-4301
- Audit log schema normalization & request_id propagation: Diego Alvarez (eng-platform) — SEC-4212
- SIEM export jobs & manifest: Sofia Martinez (eng-observability) — SEC-4350
- Attestation UI + notifications: Aisha Banerjee (security) + Product: PRD link in linked_artifacts

Unresolved / next steps:
- Confirm exact role-set definition for 'privileged' (security to propose canonical set).
- Finalize schema field names and agree on nullable vs required semantics (we should freeze by end of Jan 2026).
- Run a pilot attestation for infra + sre in Feb 2026 and gather feedback.

Notes to self / TODOs while drafting:
- Add sample NDJSON snippet and minimal RBAC CSV schema into Confluence page (avoid heavy JSON in Drive doc).
- Reach out to legal on retention and cross-border export rules for auditor bundles (GDPR concerns).
- Draft the email + Slack copy and put into /templates/attestation-email.md in repo.
